summary: @servicetitan/anvil-icons preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package's `preinstall` script runs `node setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases to a temporary directory, marks it executable, and uses that freshly-downloaded alternate runtime to execute a sibling file `math_init.js` shipped at the package root. `math_init.js` is a ~727KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle using string-array rotation and char-code decoding to hide its contents (array-rotation decoder `WV8StW`, mixed hex/string array `n7gIxM`, `_0x...`-style identifiers). The payload runs under Bun rather than Node, so it is invisible to Node-resolved code inspection. `package.json` declares `"files": ["dist", "readme.md"]` but the published tarball ships `setup.mjs` and `math_init.js` at the root and the `preinstall` hook references both — the install-time payload is outside the author's declared file manifest. An icons package has no legitimate reason to fetch a second language runtime at install time and hand it an opaque, obfuscated JS payload; the combination of alternate-runtime dropper, obfuscated payload, and files smuggled outside the declared manifest matches a compromised-publish / scope-hijack shape and gives the publisher arbitrary code execution on every installer's machine at `npm install` time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
